## Purpose

This document is a living inventory of instruments, equipment, and
major supplies maintained by the EA Program. It serves as the central
reference for locating equipment, tracking ID numbers, and linking
each item to its governing SOP. All personnel should consult this
inventory before purchasing duplicate items and should update it
whenever equipment is acquired, moved, or decommissioned.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All EA Program equipment in SGM 105, 106, 131, 132,
  133, 134, and associated field storage
- **Does not apply to:** Consumable supplies (reagents, glassware under
  $50 replacement cost), personal equipment, or equipment belonging to
  other departments
- **Maintained by:** Lab manager, with updates from all trained
  personnel


## Definitions

- **Asset tag:** A numbered label affixed to a piece of equipment to
  uniquely identify it within the EA Program inventory; the number
  should match the ID# field in this document.
- **Decommissioned:** Status assigned to equipment that has been
  permanently removed from service (broken beyond repair, surplused,
  or disposed of); must be logged with the date and reason in the
  inventory and reported to the lab manager.
- **Equipment:** In this SOP, a durable item with a replacement value
  above approximately $50 and an expected service life of more than
  one year; includes vehicles, instruments, balances, power tools,
  pumps, and major field gear.
- **ID# (inventory number):** A unique alphanumeric code assigned to
  each piece of equipment; the EA Program convention is
  `EA-[CATEGORY]-[NNN]` (e.g., EA-FLD-001 for field equipment,
  EA-LAB-001 for laboratory equipment, EA-INS-001 for analytical
  instruments); items marked *TBD* need numbers assigned at the next
  audit.
- **Related SOP:** The primary operating procedure associated with a
  piece of equipment; a dash (--) indicates no dedicated SOP exists yet.
- **TBD (to be determined):** Placeholder in the ID# or Location
  column indicating that the information needs to be confirmed during
  the next physical audit.


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab Manager       | Maintain this document; conduct annual audits; assign ID numbers |
| PI                | Approve major equipment purchases; authorize surplus or disposal |
| All Lab Personnel | Report new acquisitions, moves, or damage to the lab manager promptly |


## How to Use This Inventory

- Items marked *TBD* in the ID# column need to be assigned an
  inventory number during the next audit.
- Items marked *TBD* in the Location column need to be physically
  located and recorded.
- The Related SOP column links to the operating procedure for that
  item; a dash indicates no dedicated SOP exists yet.
- Report discrepancies (missing items, wrong locations) to the lab
  manager immediately.

## Annual Audit Procedure

1. Walk through every room listed in this inventory (SGM 105, 106,
   131, 132, 133, 134, 210) and physically verify the presence and
   condition of each item.
2. Assign an inventory ID number to any item currently marked *TBD*.
3. Update the Location column if any item has been moved.
4. Note any items that are missing, damaged, or decommissioned.
5. Add any newly acquired equipment.
6. Commit the updated file to the GitHub repository with a descriptive
   commit message.

the EA Program and whenever they are assigned responsibility for a new
class of equipment. No formal sign-off is required for this SOP.
